title: Common Operational Safety Baseline
body: This is the floor every SOP stands on — PPE, pre-op checks, hooter signals, exclusion boards, speed limits. When it slips, the failures show up as the incidents you already know: LV in the line of fire, someone approaching a machine before the operator sees them, a phone in the cab. None of those are exotic. They're baseline breaches.
keyPoints: Every operator does an FLRA before any task, must be trained and authorized, and has the right to refuse substandard conditions — that right-to-stop is the operator-level expression of the Life Saving Rules.
50 m Exclusion Boards go 50 m off the loading face AND on the ROM pad — they keep light vehicles out without authorization. This is the upstream cousin of the 50:30:10 GET rule at the crusher.
Approach rule is universal: be sure the operator has seen you, then wait for the machine parked, GET on the ground, and a signal to approach. Applies to everyone — supervisors and visitors included.
Hooter signals are fixed: 1 = start, 2 = forward, 3 = reverse. Sound it, wait for clear, then move.
Speed limits: 40 uphill haul/ramp, 30 downhill ramp, 10 tipping/hard park/workshop, 20 on the ROM pad — and slower when dust or visibility says so.
apply: On the loading face and ROM pad, confirm the 50 m exclusion boards are actually placed and standing — that single control is what stops an unauthorized LV drifting into the dig zone before anyone notices.
